haiku-low.q1: Nothing that signs the user in. It creates a pending_logins row, sets the p2f cookie, and shows the code prompt. No session exists yet.
haiku-low.q2: Only after the user confirms the pending secret with a valid code. Until then sign-in ignores pending_secret and uses the old secret.
haiku-low.q3: The server marks the code used atomically, queues a 'N remain' email, and signs in without waiting. Sign-in does not depend on the notification. The redirect goes to Security settings.
haiku-low.q4: The fifth wrong entry or 5 minutes elapsing. The server deletes the pending row, clears p2f, and returns the user to the password step.
haiku-low.q5: On confirmation, every other session of that user is deleted. The current session, identified by its sid cookie, stays.
haiku-low.q6: No. last_step is updated by a conditional UPDATE that applies only if larger, so concurrent reuse fails. Drift tolerance is one 30-second step either side.
haiku-low.q7: In one transaction: pending_secret moves to secret, old recovery codes are replaced by 10 new hashed ones, and other sessions are deleted. Partial-failure behavior is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q8: In the pending_logins table as token_hash, user_id, expires_at, attempts. The browser holds the raw token in the p2f cookie. Success, the fifth wrong entry, or expiry removes it.
haiku-low.q9: Secret: user_totp.secret, sealed. Enrolment: secret and pending_secret columns. Replay state: user_totp.last_step. Recovery codes: recovery_codes table, hashed. 2FA on means secret set and pending_secret null.
haiku-low.q10: Sign-in keeps using the old secret and old recovery codes. Cancelling clears pending_secret and leaves them untouched. If abandoned without cancelling, the pending secret sits unused.
haiku-low.q11: How the server tells the two code types apart is NOT STATED. Yes, each wrong entry of either kind increments attempts toward the limit of 5.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED. The document marks this as an open question with no designed path; support reset is undecided.

sonnet.q1: No session. The server inserts a pending_logins row (5-minute expiry, attempts=0), sets the p2f cookie, and shows the code prompt.
sonnet.q2: Once the user confirms it with a valid code: pending_secret moves into secret. Until then sign-in ignores the pending secret.
sonnet.q3: The server hashes the input, finds an unused match, and marks it used (used_at) in one atomic update. It calls enqueue_email() with a 'recovery code used, N remain' message and carries on without waiting. Sign-in does not depend on the email: a failed send is retried in the background and never blocks or fails the request. The user is then signed in via start_session() and redirected to Security settings instead of /home.
sonnet.q4: The 5th wrong entry (attempts reaches 5) or the 5-minute expiry (expires_at passing). The server deletes the pending_logins row, clears p2f, and sends the user back to the password step, where they must enter the password again.
sonnet.q5: On confirming (first setup included), the server deletes every other session of that user in the same transaction. The current session, identified by its sid cookie, stays.
sonnet.q6: No. A step already accepted for that user is rejected (any step not newer than last_step), and the conditional UPDATE stops concurrent double use. The server accepts the current 30-second time step plus one step either side (about +/-30 seconds).
sonnet.q7: In one transaction: (1) pending_secret moves into secret, (2) all old recovery codes are deleted and 10 new hashed ones inserted, (3) all other sessions of the user are deleted. The 10 plaintext codes are shown once in the response. What happens on a partial failure is NOT STATED beyond its being a single transaction.
sonnet.q8: In the pending_logins table (token_hash, user_id, expires_at, attempts). The browser holds the raw token in the p2f cookie, and only its hash is stored. It is removed on success (row deleted, p2f cleared), on the 5th wrong entry, or on expiry after 5 minutes. Expired rows are also swept periodically.
sonnet.q9: The active secret is in user_totp.secret, sealed with seal(). The pending secret is in user_totp.pending_secret, also sealed. The replay-protection state is user_totp.last_step. Recovery codes are in recovery_codes (user_id, code_hash, used_at), as hashes only, 10 per user. '2FA on' means secret is set and pending_secret is null. A replacement-pending state, with both set, also signs in using the old secret.
sonnet.q10: Sign-in keeps using the old secret, so the old authenticator still protects sign-in, and the pending secret is ignored. If the user abandons the replacement, the pending secret sits unused and the old authenticator and recovery codes stay in force. An explicit cancel clears pending_secret and also leaves the old authenticator and recovery codes untouched.
sonnet.q11: NOT STATED how the server distinguishes them. The document says only that the user enters either kind. Yes, each wrong entry of either kind increments attempts, so wrong recovery codes count toward the limit of 5.
sonnet.q12: There is none in this design. It is an open question: product has not decided whether support may reset their 2FA or how support would verify identity.
